request: We looked at December and then at November. Now compare the two months against each other by category in one picture.

plan.title: This month against last month
plan.question: Spending of this month and of last month per category, one row per category and period, the period named 'This month' or 'Last month', the six largest categories by total over both months, columns topic, period and total_eur.

sql:
WITH picked AS (
  SELECT coalesce(category, 'Needs review') AS topic, -SUM(amount) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND booked_on >= '2025-11-01' AND booked_on < '2026-01-01'
  GROUP BY topic
  ORDER BY spent DESC
  LIMIT 6
)
SELECT picked.topic AS topic,
       CASE WHEN transaction_view.booked_on >= '2025-12-01' THEN 'This month' ELSE 'Last month' END AS period,
       ROUND(-SUM(transaction_view.amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
JOIN picked ON picked.topic = coalesce(transaction_view.category, 'Needs review')
WHERE transaction_view.amount < 0
  AND transaction_view.booked_on >= '2025-11-01' AND transaction_view.booked_on < '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY topic, period
ORDER BY topic, period
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
the two earlier turns named December and November, so this turn inherits both months
two periods compared by category are two dimensions that cross, so grouped bars
the category is the position and the period is the series, so the rows come long
the columns are topic, period and total_eur, the euro column last
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_grouped, so barY carries a series and layout: group()
the columns are topic, period and total_eur, and total_eur holds the numbers
period is the series, so it is the z and the color channel and the legend goes on
category names on x on a band scale, tilted and none dropped, euros on y from the bare factory
